items.title: Some think Britain's 'broken', and they are looking to Australia for inspiration
items.description: Right-wing populism is rising in the UK where, like Australia, the political landscape is looking very different lately. It has prompted some people to ask if these surging parties can deliver on their promises.

items.title: These women are harvesting our food. Why are they giving birth in secret?
items.description: For the Pacific Islander women who harvest the fruit and vegetables that stock Australia’s supermarket shelves, motherhood here can mean injury, debt, secrecy and fear.

items.title: As the US marks defeating a king, Trump consumes Washington
items.description: Project by project, Donald Trump is altering the United States capital, and in some cases, disrupting views and design that date back more than two centuries.

items.title: 'Who will be accountable for this?': Families grieve sailors killed in Strait of Hormuz
items.description: Families of Indian sailors who died in a US military attack in the Strait of Hormuz want to know who is accountable for attacks on commercial vessels.

items.title: Nine-year-old Australian girl fatally shot by police in Pakistan
items.description: A nine-year-old Australian girl has been fatally shot by police in Pakistan after officers mistook her family's car for that of suspected criminals.

items.title: Live: Brazil and Morocco trade brilliant goals in star-studded clash
items.description: Brazil meets Morocco in a blockbuster clash after Qatar salvaged a late draw against Switzerland in San Francisco, while later Haiti faces Scotland. Follow live.

items.title: Here's what you need to know about the KPMG scandal
items.description: Accounting firm KPMG is engulfed in a scandal that has seen several senior leaders quit and ASIC launch an investigation into the firm's business dealings.

items.title: How this globe shows the incredibly diverse story of our Socceroos
items.description: The Socceroos squad is like no other that's ever been sent to represent us at a World Cup. See the extraordinary journeys that forged a team to represent modern Australia on the world stage.

items.title: The multi-million-dollar tourist hotspot where locals can't afford to live
items.description: A tourist hotspot with skyrocketing rents, low rental vacancies and a dearth of public housing, has found a way to help find homes for those who can't afford to live in their own region.

items.title: Pakistan says Iran-US peace deal is within 24 hours, Tehran urges caution
items.description: Lebanon's state media has reported Israeli strikes on the country's south, as Pakistan says a US-Iran peace deal signing is expected within 24 hours.

items.title: Why older Australians with MND are considering early euthanasia
items.description: The death of AFL legend Neale Daniher has shone a light on the grim choices faced by older Australians fighting motor neurone disease.

items.title: Qld couple who made $40 million MND donation are 'not trying to be philanthropists'
items.description: Quentin and Kylie Birt say they were inspired to donate at the Big Freeze event after reading Neale Daniher's book.

items.title: Liberal frontbencher Jonno Duniam to retire
items.description: Senator Duniam says it is time to prioritise his family after 25 years in politics, and he will leave his position in the Senate by the end of this year.

items.title: Tinariwen deliver songs of hope from a homeland in crisis
items.description: Legendary African band Tinariwen say there’s very little hope for their country. It just makes their dedication to music more important.

items.title: Can you soar to the top of this week's spelling quiz?
items.description: From homophones to Aussie bird names, Guy Montgomery's Spelling Bee quiz is set to test and teach in equal measure.

items.title: Street signs link coastal town and luxury ocean liners dating back to 1800s
items.description: Orient Point, where the streets are named after ships beginning with "O", shows how national pride in 19th and early 20th-century boatbuilding featured in colonial town planning.

items.title: Why young people say the social media ban is not working six months on
items.description: Research suggests many under-16s are still active on social media platforms. BTN High explores why and tests the accuracy of popular technology used to estimate age.

items.title: A cafe run by students, for students aims to tackle food insecurity
items.description: It might look like a regular cafe, but a new student-run business in Hobart's CBD has a different goal than turning a profit — a mission to feed their struggling peers.

items.title: 'Straight to landfill': Compostable packaging but nowhere to compost it
items.description: The ACT mandates reusable, recyclable and compostable packaging at all public events, but nearly all of it ends up in landfill because there is no facility to compost it.

items.title: T-Birds cap off near-flawless season with record number of wins
items.description: This year's record-breaking Adelaide Thunderbirds are shifting their focus to the Super Netball finals, with a third premiership in four years on offer.

items.title: 'We need to review': Piastri drops down in qualifying despite fast start
items.description: Oscar Piastri will start seventh in the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix despite a fast start in qualifying that had him on track for pole.

items.title: Pint-sized superheroes find love for art via creative gallery program
items.description: This group of pint-sized superheroes is taking part in an early childhood education tour run by the Art Gallery of NSW, which teaches young minds about shapes, colour and form.

items.title: Body of girl recovered from Sydney bay where father was found dead
items.description: Police divers have recovered the body of a young girl from a bay in Sydney's inner west.

items.title: Early childhood educators burnt out, stretched and 'paid peanuts'
items.description: Early childhood operators say increased load on educators is taking a "huge toll" on their mental health and safety.

items.title: Two mates, one chair: travelling the world with paraplegia and a best friend
items.description: Best friends Lachie and Fletcher have nailed the art of ignoring what people think, travelling the world as Two Mates, 1 Chair.
